title: Aggregation Artifacts in Subjective Tasks Collapse Large Language Models’ Posteriors
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure any aspect of faith or religion. It evaluates model performance on subjective tasks, specifically multilabel emotion recognition and morality recognition using the Moral Foundation Reddit Corpus (MFRC). The moral foundations measured are care, equality, proportionality, loyalty, authority, and purity, treated as psychological constructs rather than religious ones.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its findings focus on how aggregating subjective annotations from different individuals creates artifacts that hinder Large Language Model performance in tasks like emotion and morality recognition. It suggests that models perform better when learning from individual annotators, especially minority-viewpoint annotators, rather than from an aggregated 'crowd truth'.
